title: Do Emergent Misalignment Models Share a Circuit?
abstract: arXiv:2610.20887v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Fine-tuning language models on narrowly defined harmful tasks can induce emergent misalignment (EM) across unrelated domains. While prior work has identified shared misalignment-associated representations across independently fine-tuned models, it remains unclear whether these models rely on common computational components. We investigate this question using three LoRA fine-tunes of Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct trained on harmful medical advice, risky financial advice, and extreme-sports recommendations. Using direction-based activation tracing, we identify three attention-head locations shared among the five highest-ranked heads of all three organisms. Replacing each organism's five selected head contributions with Base contributions reduces free-generation EM from 38.9% to 22.9% for medical, 50.7% to 12.5% for finance, and 41.7% to 11.1% for sports, outperforming layer-matched random interventions without reducing judged coherence. translated_title: 涌现失对齐模型是否共享同一电路？
translated_abstract: 在狭义定义的有害任务上对语言模型进行微调，可能在无关领域诱发涌现性失对齐。尽管先前的工作已在各自独立微调的模型中识别出共享的与失对齐相关的表示，但这些模型是否依赖共同的计算组件仍不清楚。我们使用三个基于 Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct 的 LoRA 微调模型来研究这个问题，它们分别在有害医疗建议、高风险金融建议和极限运动推荐任务上训练。通过基于方向的激活追踪，我们在所有三个模型体排名前五的注意力头中识别出三个共享的注意力头位置。将每个模型体所选的五个注意力头的贡献替换为基础模型的贡献后，自由生成中的涌现失对齐率从医疗领域的 38.9% 降至 22.9%，金融领域从 50.7% 降至 12.5%，体育领域从 41.7% 降至 11.1%，其效果优于层级匹配的随机干预，且不会降低被评判的连贯性。
tldr: 研究发现在不同有害任务上独立微调得到的涌现失对齐模型共享相同的注意力头电路，将这些头的贡献替换为基础模型的贡献即可大幅降低失对齐行为且不损害连贯性。
en_tdlr: Emergently misaligned models fine-tuned on different harmful tasks share common attention-head circuits, and replacing these heads' contributions with base model contributions substantially reduces misalignment without sacrificing coherence.
